external_blockers.description: vm.overcommit_memory=0, requires sudo (no passwordless sudo available)
external_blockers.exact_command: sudo sysctl -w vm.overcommit_memory=1 && echo 'vm.overcommit_memory = 1' | sudo tee /etc/sysctl.d/99-redis-overcommit.conf && sudo sysctl --system

external_blockers.description: Installed rq==1.15.1, Frappe pyproject.toml declares rq (2.10.0). Root cause of datetime.utcnow() deprecation warnings. Upgrading affects the whole bench's job queue -- not performed without explicit approval per 'no uncontrolled upgrades' rule.
external_blockers.status: documented, non-blocking (deprecation warning only, does not stop scheduler/worker)

resolved_blockers.resolution: Resolved 2026-07-18. The accesslint MCP's bundled Chrome launcher could not become CDP-debuggable in this container, but Linux-native Playwright Chromium (installed fresh via npx playwright install chromium) worked cleanly on first attempt -- no environment changes needed. Root cause was specific to that one launcher, not a fundamental container limitation.

known_hardening_items_not_fixed_in_this_.description: Losing side of a concurrent stock reservation race gets a raw QueryDeadlockError (500-class) on first attempt instead of a friendly 'N units remain, retry?' message. A retry succeeds correctly with the true remaining quantity. Data-safety guarantee (never over-reserve) holds regardless.
known_hardening_items_not_fixed_in_this_.recommendation: Wrap create_stock_reservation_entries() call site with a bounded retry-on-deadlock loop (catch pymysql error 1213, retry once with short backoff).
known_hardening_items_not_fixed_in_this_.why_not_fixed_now: Out of scope for a verification mission to silently modify core reservation call-site behavior; flagged for a deliberate future hardening pass.

incidents.description: During BLOCKER-003 investigation (before this Phase 6 batch), a cleanup step used `taskkill /F /IM chrome.exe` (by image name) instead of a specific PID, closing all of the user's real Chrome windows on the Windows host.
incidents.disclosure: Told to the user immediately in the same turn it happened, with an apology and a stop on further Windows process actions.
incidents.corrective_action: This Phase 6 batch's explicit rules forbade Windows Chrome, /mnt/c/, and any wildcard process kill entirely -- followed throughout with zero incidents. All browser PIDs this batch were Linux-native Playwright processes, closed via .close()/.close() and verified gone via `ps -p`.
